ideas.description: Exploit by stacking two near-misses. On E038 (2x20+3x24+2x28+4x32 px, 2/3/3, Muon with AOL plus 2 NS steps, conv1 block frozen at 32 px, ls 0.4; 6.68 s), make two changes. (1) Re-apply E042's pooling cut: replace the head's AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) with x.flatten(2).max(dim=2).values at every resolution and in eval. Use the indices-based backward, not amax, because amax crashed in E041. (2) Add E043's end-of-train BN re-estimation with 4 batches instead of 6. After the final Lookahead sync, reset all BN running stats. Re-estimate them with momentum=None from 4 forward-only batches of 1536 un-augmented 32 px training images, drawn with the trial-seeded generator, under no_grad, fp16 and channels_last. Then restore BN momentum. Put the re-estimation pass in a small graph or compiled function warmed up in build on synthetic data. Recapture all 4 train graphs in build. Check that eval gives finite [B,100] logits for B in {1, 7, 513, 1024}. Besides the official run, evaluate the same code on dev seeds 3-12 outside the official command, so the BN-re-estimation gain is measured against E046's 10-seed baseline of 0.7534 with SE about 0.09 pp, not against a single draw.
ideas.expected: Time about 6.52-6.58 s, down 1.5-2.4% from 6.68 s: -0.19 s from pooling and +0.04-0.05 s for 4 re-estimation batches. Official 3-seed accuracy 0.7525-0.757. Dev 10-seed mean 0.7535-0.7555, centred near +0.1 pp over 0.7534. Keep if official >=0.7535 and dev mean >=0.753. A dev gain >=0.1 pp supports the BN-mismatch part of H2.3.2 and makes this the margin base for the 28 px freeze and bias-window cuts. A dev gain <0.03 pp refutes it: then drop the re-estimation and re-apply the pooling cut alone with the next margin source.

ideas.description: Exploit, removing low-res backward work at a phase boundary, so no new graph is needed. On the current tip (idea A's stack if kept, else E038 plus the pooling cut), train the whitening-conv bias only during the 20 px phase (epochs 1-2, about 64 steps) instead of epochs 1-5. In the 24 px phase, detach the whitening output (after its activation) before group 1, as the 28/32 px graphs already do, and zero the whitening bias lr or drop it from that phase's parameter list. The 24 px graph is recaptured in build with the detach. The 20 px graph is unchanged and the graph count stays 4. This is the 2-epoch window between E045's 8 steps (failed, -0.47 pp) and E029's 3 epochs (neutral), aligned with the 20->24 px boundary. Also evaluate dev seeds 3-12. Log ms/step in the 24 px phase.
ideas.expected: 24 px ms/step falls about 3-5%, so total time falls about 0.04-0.07 s (-0.6 to -1%). This is removed work, so it should carry over to the PCIe judge. Dev 10-seed mean within ±0.1 pp of the base. Keep if official >=0.7535, dev mean >=0.753 and time is >=0.5% lower. If the dev mean falls by >=0.2 pp, the bias needs the 24 px phase. Then the window lies between 2 and 3 epochs and H2.4.8 is closed as not worth a graph.

ideas.description: Exploit, extending the FreezeOut-style cut. On the current tip (idea A's stack if kept, else E038 plus the pooling cut), also freeze the first group-1 conv block (whitening-output -> 128 conv, pool, BN, GELU) during the 2 epochs at 28 px, exactly as already done at 32 px. In the 28 px graph, detach the block's output before the second group-1 conv. Drop that conv's weight and BN affine params from the 28 px phase's Muon/SGD lists, or zero their lr. BN stays in train mode. Recapture the 28 px graph in build; the graph count is unchanged. conv1 is then trained only in the 5 epochs at 20/24 px. Evaluate dev seeds 3-12 alongside the official run. Log ms/step per phase.
ideas.expected: 28 px ms/step falls 5-8%, so total time falls about 0.07-0.11 s (-1 to -1.7%), to about 6.45-6.5 s if stacked on idea A. Dev 10-seed mean -0.0 to -0.2 pp, centred near -0.08 pp. Keep if official >=0.7535 and dev mean >=0.753 (H2.4.6's base-margin condition). If the dev mean drops by >=0.2 pp, conv1 still needs the near-full-res updates: refute H2.4.6 and keep the freeze at 32 px only.

ideas.description: Exploit, buying margin through the smallest group-3 capacity step. Before the official run, microbenchmark ms/step per phase on the current recipe (graphed, Muon included) for group-3 widths 576 and 640. Do not reuse E004/E044 deltas: the E044 post-mortem showed that the cost structure has shifted. If 640 costs <=+4% ms/step, then on the current tip (with the pooling cut) widen group 3 from 576 to 640 at every resolution and adjust the head input. Hold epochs, resolutions, LR schedule, Muon lr/momentum, ls, freezing and the bias window fixed. Recapture all graphs in build. Run official seeds plus dev seeds 3-12. If the microbenchmark shows >+5%, log it and do not run.
ideas.expected: ms/step +2.5-4%, so time about +0.17-0.25 s over the pooling-cut base (about 6.68-6.75 s; roughly equal to E038 without the pooling cut). Dev 10-seed mean +0.1 to +0.25 pp, centred near +0.17 pp (E044's 768 gave +0.4 pp on one draw). If the dev gain is >=0.2 pp at <=+4% time, H6.1.3 is supported, and this becomes the margin base that the 28 px shift (E037) and the 28 px freeze are spent against. A dev gain <0.1 pp means group-3 capacity is only useful at large widths: close H6.1.

ideas.description: Explore an SGD-era knob never varied under Muon. Note: with per-step weight renorm, weight decay on the Muon conv group is effectively a no-op, so the live knobs are the SGD-group settings. On E038 (or the current tip), halve the BN-bias lr multiplier from 64x to 32x, and change nothing else. Keep Muon lr/momentum, head lr, wd, the schedule and Lookahead fixed. The multiplier lives in the per-group lr. If it is folded into the GPU schedule tensor, no recapture is needed; otherwise recapture in build. Evaluate dev seeds 3-12 plus official seeds. Contingency: if the dev mean falls by >=0.15 pp, run 128x next.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Dev 10-seed mean moves -0.3 to +0.3 pp with no strong prior. The multiplier was tuned for Nesterov SGD at batch 1024, lr 9.0, and the SGD groups have since been rescaled linearly for batch 1536. A |delta| >=0.15 pp supports H1.7.12 and sets the direction. Keep if the dev gain is >=0.1 pp and official >=0.7535. A |delta| <0.1 pp closes the SGD-group knobs as margin sources.

structured_output.summary:
Where things stand: E046 put the E038 tip at a 10-seed mean of 0.7534 (per-seed std 0.28 pp) and showed that identical code reproduces bit-for-bit. So a single official draw at >=0.7535 is acceptable again, and dev seeds 3-12 now give about 0.09 pp SE per config. That is cheaper and sharper than salts, so every new margin idea measures its gain on dev seeds as well as on the official run.

New ideas (5, which brings the queue to 7):
- Top priority (exploit) combines two earlier near-misses: the banked -0.19 s pooling cut from E042 and a cheaper 4-batch version of E043's BN re-estimation. Expected time is about 6.55 s, and the run also measures how much accuracy the BN re-estimation really adds (H2.3.2).
- Two removed-work cuts to stack on that base:
  - Whitening-bias window limited to the 20 px phase, with the whitening output detached at 24 px (H2.4.8). The cut lines up with a phase boundary, so the graph count does not change.
  - The conv1-block freeze extended to the 28 px phase (H2.4.6).
- One capacity step: group 3 at 640 channels (H6.1.3), run only if a microbenchmark on the current recipe shows ms/step rising by no more than 4%. This is the lesson from E044.
- One free explore: the BN-bias lr multiplier halved to 32x (H1.7.12). Weight decay on the Muon convs is effectively a no-op under the per-step weight renorm, so only the SGD-group settings are live knobs here.

Kept as queued: I054 (Polar Express, H1.7.9) and I055 (head output scale, H1.3.4). Both test open hypotheses and add no time. I053 is still running. Nothing is dropped.

Not queued, and why:
- Group-2 depth cut (H2.4.7): not worth running while the recipe looks capacity-limited (H6).
- Muon renorm every k steps (H2.5.3) and whole-run CUDA graph (H2.5.4): overhead-type cuts that may not carry over to the PCIe judge (H5.1).
- Anchor-fixed epoch tests (H1.8.2, H1.9.1): at best about 0.35 pp/s, which is too expensive to help the score.
